skill.name: colorize
skill.description: Add strategic color to features that are too monochromatic or lack visual interest. Makes interfaces more engaging and expressive.
skill.summary: Adds purposeful color to interfaces while preserving hierarchy, accessibility, and brand fit.
skill.author: pbakaus

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown inline color values and design assessment wording. No executable commands, host reconnaissance, data collection, or prompt injection attempts were found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - **Tinted backgrounds**: Replace pure gray (`#f5f5f5`) with warm neutrals (`oklch(97% 0.01 60)`) or
- Use pure black (`#000`) or pure white (`#fff`) for large areas
- **Color absence**: Pure grayscale? Limited neutrals? One timid accent?

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 75 uses Markdown inline code for color values such as hex and OKLCH examples. There is no shell, Ruby execution, or command invocation.
Line 129 uses Markdown inline code for color literals. It does not execute commands or construct a command string.
Line 24 asks the user to assess color use in a design. This is UI design context gathering, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Many interfaces feel flat when they rely on gray surfaces and weak accents. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code add color with purpose, hierarchy, and accessibility.
actual_capabilities: Identifies where color can add hierarchy, semantic meaning, wayfinding, and visual warmth.
Plans a restrained palette with a dominant color, accent colors, and usage rationale.
Guides semantic colors for success, error, warning, info, status badges, and progress indicators.
Applies color to buttons, links, icons, backgrounds, surfaces, borders, typography, and charts.
Checks contrast, color vision accessibility, consistent meanings, and balanced color distribution.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not a standalone color engine or visual testing tool.
It depends on existing brand colors, product context, or user-provided design direction.
It may require a companion frontend design workflow before implementation starts.
It cannot guarantee WCAG compliance without testing the rendered interface.

use_cases.title: Revive a Grayscale Dashboard
use_cases.description: Add semantic status colors, chart colors, and action emphasis without making the dashboard noisy.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Color System
use_cases.description: Define where brand colors, accent colors, and neutral tints should appear across a feature.

use_cases.title: Improve Design Token Usage
use_cases.description: Review color roles and replace arbitrary values with a consistent, accessible palette.

prompt_templates.title: Colorize a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused UI update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the colorize skill on this component. Keep the palette restrained and explain where each color adds meaning.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Semantic Palette
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for state and category colors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the colorize skill to define success, error, warning, info, and neutral colors for this feature.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh a Product Area
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a multi-screen interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the colorize skill across this product area. Preserve brand fit, improve hierarchy, and avoid random decoration.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Refine Color Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for design system alignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the colorize skill to audit current color usage, identify inconsistencies, and propose accessible design token updates.

output_examples.input: A gray analytics dashboard with muted buttons and hard-to-scan status labels.
output_examples.output: The result uses one primary accent for actions, semantic badge colors for status, and softer tinted surfaces for section grouping.

output_examples.input: A settings page that uses only black, white, and gray.
output_examples.output: The result adds a warm neutral background, colored focus states, and restrained accents on important controls.

output_examples.input: A project board where task types and progress states look identical.
output_examples.output: The result assigns consistent colors to task categories, progress states, and priority markers while preserving contrast.

best_practices: Start from existing brand colors before adding new accents.
Use bright color mainly for important actions, states, and navigation cues.
Validate text contrast and avoid relying on color alone.
anti_patterns: Adding many unrelated colors to make a screen feel lively.
Using color without semantic meaning or hierarchy.
Applying pure black or pure white across large interface areas.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps add strategic color to interfaces that feel too monochrome, flat, or visually unclear.

faq.question: Does it choose random colors?
faq.answer: No. It asks for context and applies color based on brand fit, hierarchy, meaning, and accessibility.

faq.question: Can it work with existing design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can align color choices with existing tokens, brand palettes, and component roles.

faq.question: Does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: It prompts for contrast checks, color vision review, and non-color indicators for important states.

faq.question: Can it improve charts and dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers data visualization colors, status colors, progress indicators, and visual hierarchy.

faq.question: Is it only for colorful brands?
faq.answer: No. It can add subtle warmth and structure while keeping a restrained product style.
